newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended a busy week with another day of heavy trade that saw the industrials index hit a new high as local buyers poured into the market, dealers said.
The market has been boosted by speculation that interest rate cuts are in the offing sooner rather than later, in marked contrast to the trend in other major financial markets.
The bull runs being enjoyed by global bourses in New York and Europe have also boosted sentiment, following upbeat comments earlier in the week by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
"It was another hectic day with a little offshore buying, but mostly just good two way local trade," one dealer said.
The industrials index added to a record set on Thursday by climbing to another new high of 9,054.4, up 28.1 points, as the all-share index gained 17.0 points to 7,444.0.

The gold index posted some healthy gains as it continued to react to the vagaries of the bullion price and got a boost from the yellow metal's stability around $323 a ounce. The golds index put on 17.2 points, or 1.8 percent, to 969.8.
Dealers said expectations of a continued rally in South Africa's bond market and interest rate cut hopes would lift Johannesburg industrial shares to fresh peaks next week.

Sectors sensitive to rate movements, including stores, banking and construction, were expected to benefit most, taking the industrial index to new highs ahead of an expected reduction in the country's high lending rates. Highly geared firms also stood to gain strongly.
"I am bullish on industrials and the bond market," said Peer Iuel, managing director of UAL Securities.

Trade on the day was heavy with around 1.36 billion rands worth of business being conducted. Big name stocks attracted the most interest, with Capital Alliance losing 50 cents to 36.00 rand in trade worth 172 million rand.
Gencor saw trade worth 64 million rand as market attention perked after its Billiton listing on the London bourse. Gencor ended off 35 cents to 18.45 rand.
Drinks giant SA Breweries was the second biggest trader on the day with stocks worth 83 million rand flowing through the market. The firm ended up 250 cents to 143.50 rand.
Other individual shares that caught dealers' eyes included electronics to healthcare firm Jasco Electronics which soared on speculation that a deal was imminent. Jasco added 54 cents to 280 cents.
A source close to the company said there was something in the pipeline but declined to give further details.

East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd sank to a year-low of 70 cents in active early trade after the gold producer warned late on Thursday there was a strong possibility that it could close. But the stock recovered to end one cent up at 101 cents.
JCI Ltd gained 100 cents to 31.25 rand after news broke it had sold its shares in Britain's Johnson Matthey to possibly help funds its buy of a Lonrho stake.
"(The Johnson Matthey cash) could be used in that respect, but that is a decision that doesn't have to be taken yet," a JCI spokesman told Reuters.

Analysts had been expecting the Johnson Matthey sale and are also speculating on other options such as the sale or merger of its unlisted Tavistock coal division with Lonrho and the disposal of non-core assets such as a 9.8 percent stake in Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
In the futures market trade was more subdued with near-dated contracts nudging up in line the share market.
The September golds contract was last at 674/78 from 669 as the industrials contract was at 8,616/20 from 8,589. The all-share contract was at 6,708/13 from 6,693.
